newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia to set rules for government bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Estonia to set rules for government bond issues.

text.p: The Estonian goverment is to prepare the legal framework for the government to issue bonds although no issue is planned at the moment, Finance Minister Mart Opmann said on Thursday.

Estonia's government has to have a balanced budget and has so far not made any issue of debt instruments either at home or abroad. The council of capital city Tallinn earlier this year raised 60 million marks with a three-year bond.
"We do not have any intention to issue them right now, but there is plenty of free money in the Estonian market and why not use it instead of foreign loans," Opmann told a news conference.
Enn Pant, a finance ministry adviser, said that loans from the World Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) involved a bureaucratic procedure.
"If we borrow money from the internal market, then we escape currency risk, lure back the money that Estonian banks keep abroad and strengthen domestic banking," Pant added.
There is little debt paper available in Estonia apart from some commercial paper issues by local corporates.
